record.context_brief: Sequences, locally free of arithmetic progressions
record.original_question: Fix an integer s 3 and suppose that A = fa1; a2; : : :g is a strictly increasing sequence of non-negative integers, such that no segment of this sequence of the form (ai+1; ai+2; : : :; ai+s) for i = 0; 1; : : : contains a three-term arithmetic progression. How large can the density of A be under this assumption? The contributor observes that for s = 4 one can take A = f0; 1; 3; 4; 6; 7; 9; 10; : : :g (the set of all non-negative integers, congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 3) with the density 2=3; similarly, for s = 8 one can take A = f0; 1; 3; 4; 9; 10; 12; 13; 18; 19; 21;: : :g (the set of all non-negative integers, congruent to 0; 1; 3, or 4 modulo 9) with the density 4=9. Konyagin indicates that if n(s) denotes the smallest positive integer N such that there exists an s-element subset of [1; N], free of three-term arithmetic progressions, then the upper asymptotic density of A does not exceed s=n(s); on the other hand, there exists A with the property in question and with the lower asymptotic density at least s=(2n(s)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $s \geq 3$ be a fixed integer. Call a strictly increasing sequence $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < \dots\}$ of non-negative integers $s$-locally AP-free if for every $i \geq 0$ the consecutive block $(a_{i+1}, a_{i+2}, \dots, a_{i+s})$ contains no three-term arithmetic progression (i.e., no three indices $i+1 \leq j_1 < j_2 < j_3 \leq i+s$ with $a_{j_1} + a_{j_3} = 2 a_{j_2}$).

For such a sequence $A$, let
$$\overline{d}(A) = \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{|A \cap [0,N]|}{N+1}, \qquad \underline{d}(A) = \liminf_{N \to \infty} \frac{|A \cap [0,N]|}{N+1}.$$

Determine
$$D(s) := \sup\{\overline{d}(A) : A \text{ is } s\text{-locally AP-free}\}.$$

It is known that if $n(s)$ denotes the smallest positive integer $N$ such that $[1,N]$ contains an $s$-element subset free of three-term arithmetic progressions, then every $s$-locally AP-free sequence $A$ satisfies $\overline{d}(A) \leq s/n(s)$, and there exist $s$-locally AP-free sequences with $\underline{d}(A) \geq s/(2 n(s))$. For example, for $s = 4$ one has $D(4) \geq 2/3$ (achieved by integers congruent to $0$ or $1$ modulo $3$), and for $s = 8$ one has $D(8) \geq 4/9$ (achieved by integers congruent to $0,1,3$, or $4$ modulo $9$). Find the exact value of $D(s)$ for all $s \geq 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a problem of Freiman from a collection of open problems in additive combinatorics. Only the bounds $s/(2 n(s)) \le D(s) \le s/n(s)$ (with $n(s)$ the smallest $N$ such that $[1,N]$ contains an $s$-element AP-3-free subset) appear to be known, and no exact formula for $D(s)$ has been established. The problem is generally regarded as open.
